findings.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:14-30 — TopicEmbed.import does read-then-write (where(embed_url:).first then create!) with no locking/find_or_create_or upsert, so concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic jobs processing the same URL race and one raises an unrescued RecordInvalid/RecordNotUnique from the unique index, aborting the transaction instead of being handled as "already imported".

lib/topic_retriever.rb:38-46 — perform_retrieve checks TopicEmbed.exists? then calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inline inside a regular job and checks exists? again, but this reimplements the same racy read-then-write path as TopicEmbed.import and can also fetch/parse the entire feed synchronously inside a request-triggered job just to resolve one embed_url.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24-25 — SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) performs an unbounded, untimed-out synchronous HTTP fetch of an external, admin-controlled URL inside a scheduled Sidekiq job with sidekiq_options retry: false, so a slow/hanging remote server stalls the worker for the life of the request with no retry recovery.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:38-46 — import_remote does open(url).read to fetch arbitrary external content synchronously with no timeout/size bound, called from both the scheduled poll path and the per-request RetrieveTopic job, risking worker/job hangs and unbounded memory use on large or slow responses.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3-10 — topic_id and post_id columns are plain integers with null: false but no foreign key constraint and no index on topic_id/post_id (only embed_url is indexed), so TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: post.topic_id) lookups and topic/post associations rely on unindexed columns and DB-level referential integrity is not enforced, allowing orphaned embeds if a topic/post is destroyed.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:5-6 — validates_presence_of :embed_url plus the DB unique index only guarantees uniqueness/non-blankness of the string, not that it is a well-formed absolute URL; the actual invariant enforced by callers (url =~ /^https?\:\/\// in .import) is checked ad hoc before save rather than as a model validation, so a TopicEmbed could be created directly (e.g. via console or future code path) with a non-http embed_url that passes validation.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError on nil for feeds without a content field (e.g. RSS description-only items), and with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the whole poll run is silently dropped with no test covering this path (confidence 75, P2).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — `rss.items.each do |i|` has no per-item begin/rescue, so one malformed item (bad link, nil content) aborts processing of all remaining feed items for that poll cycle (confidence 60, P2).

app/models/topic_embed.rb:39 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `import_remote` has no rescue for network failures (404/timeout/SSL) from open-uri; an unhandled exception propagates out of the async RetrieveTopic job with no explicit error handling or logging (confidence 55, P2).

app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — `absolutize_urls` treats protocol-relative URLs (e.g. `//evil.com/x`) as root-relative via `start_with?('/')`, producing a mangled URL (`prefix + "/" + "evil.com/x"`) instead of leaving it absolute or handling it correctly (confidence 65, P3).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34-35 — if both `i.link` and `i.id` are blank/non-http, the resulting url fails the regex check inside `TopicEmbed.import` and the item is silently skipped with no logging, so failed imports are unobservable (confidence 50, P3).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content.scrub` calls String#scrub, which was only added in Ruby 2.1 (Dec 2013), but the Gemfile targets Ruby 1.9/2.0 ("perftools only works on 1.9 atm"), so this will raise NoMethodError on every feed poll under the app's actual runtime. confidence:75 severity:P1

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:14-30 — TopicEmbed.import does read-then-write (where(embed_url:).first then create!) with no locking/find_or_create_or upsert, so concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic jobs processing the same URL race and one raises an unrescued RecordInvalid/RecordNotUnique from the unique index, aborting the transaction instead of being handled as "already imported".

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-insert: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!(...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so two concurrent workers (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` iterating items and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` fetching the same `embed_url`) can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`. The loser will raise an unhandled DB uniqueness error (`RecordNotUnique`), aborting the transaction and bubbling up since neither `import` nor the calling jobs rescue it. This matches the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:38-46 — perform_retrieve checks TopicEmbed.exists? then calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inline inside a regular job and checks exists? again, but this reimplements the same racy read-then-write path as TopicEmbed.import and can also fetch/parse the entire feed synchronously inside a request-triggered job just to resolve one embed_url.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve does a check-then-act pattern: it returns if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?, then (if feed polling is enabled) runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously and checks exists? again, and finally may call TopicEmbed.import_remote. This is verifiably synchronous (it instantiates and calls execute directly, not enqueue), and PollFeed#poll_feed fetches/parses the entire feed and iterates all items, which is potentially expensive even though the retriever is trying to satisfy a single embed_url. Separately, TopicEmbed.import itself is also check-then-create (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first then TopicEmbed.create!), with a unique index on embed_url; concurrent retriever executions can pass the exists?/where checks and both attempt create!, leading to a real race that can raise a uniqueness violation without rescue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24-25 — SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) performs an unbounded, untimed-out synchronous HTTP fetch of an external, admin-controlled URL inside a scheduled Sidekiq job with sidekiq_options retry: false, so a slow/hanging remote server stalls the worker for the life of the request with no retry recovery.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the new PollFeed job does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no timeout options. Ruby's open-uri/Net::HTTP defaults do not enforce open/read timeouts unless explicitly provided, so a slow or hanging remote feed endpoint can block the Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely during this synchronous fetch. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so there is no retry mechanism to recover once a run fails, and a hang stalls the worker for the duration of the hang.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:38-46 — import_remote does open(url).read to fetch arbitrary external content synchronously with no timeout/size bound, called from both the scheduled poll path and the per-request RetrieveTopic job, risking worker/job hangs and unbounded memory use on large or slow responses.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import_remote the code does `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no explicit timeouts, redirect limits, or response size bounds, then passes the full body into Readability. This is a synchronous network fetch that can block a Sidekiq worker thread and can allocate unbounded memory on large/slow responses. It is invoked from TopicRetriever#fetch_http, which is run by the async `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job (enqueued from EmbedController when an embed is missing). The finding’s core concern is therefore directly supported by the diff (even though PollFeed itself calls `open(feed_url)` and uses TopicEmbed.import, not import_remote).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3-10 — topic_id and post_id columns are plain integers with null: false but no foreign key constraint and no index on topic_id/post_id (only embed_url is indexed), so TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: post.topic_id) lookups and topic/post associations rely on unindexed columns and DB-level referential integrity is not enforced, allowing orphaned embeds if a topic/post is destroyed.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id` and `post_id` as plain integer columns and only adds a unique index on `embed_url`. There are no indexes on `topic_id` or `post_id` in the diff, so queries filtering `topic_embeds` by those columns (e.g., `TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: ...)` as shown in the spec) would require a table scan as the table grows. The diff also does not add any DB-level foreign key constraints for those columns, so the database would not prevent orphaned `topic_embeds` rows if referenced topics/posts are deleted (whether that happens depends on other code not shown, but the lack of FK constraints itself is verifiable).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:5-6 — validates_presence_of :embed_url plus the DB unique index only guarantees uniqueness/non-blankness of the string, not that it is a well-formed absolute URL; the actual invariant enforced by callers (url =~ /^https?\:\/\// in .import) is checked ad hoc before save rather than as a model validation, so a TopicEmbed could be created directly (e.g. via console or future code path) with a non-http embed_url that passes validation.

adjudication.rationale: In the new TopicEmbed model, only `validates_presence_of :embed_url` is added, and the migration adds a unique index on `embed_url`. Neither enforces that `embed_url` is a well-formed absolute http(s) URL. The only format check is the regex guard in `TopicEmbed.import` (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`), which is a caller-side check and can be bypassed by creating a TopicEmbed directly (e.g., `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: 'foo', ...)`), which would pass model validations and DB constraints. This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — `rss.items.each do |i|` has no per-item begin/rescue, so one malformed item (bad link, nil content) aborts processing of all remaining feed items for that poll cycle (confidence 60, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the loop `rss.items.each do |i|` calls `i.content.scrub` unconditionally. If a feed item lacks `content` (nil) or has an unexpected type, this will raise (e.g., NoMethodError), and because there is no per-item rescue, the exception will abort the entire poll and prevent remaining items from being processed in that cycle. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:39 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `import_remote` has no rescue for network failures (404/timeout/SSL) from open-uri; an unhandled exception propagates out of the async RetrieveTopic job with no explicit error handling or logging (confidence 55, P2).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code calls `open(url).read` (open-uri) without any `rescue`. This can raise on common network/HTTP issues (timeouts, DNS, SSL errors, non-2xx responses depending on open-uri behavior) and nothing in `import_remote`, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, or `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` rescues those exceptions. As a result, failures will bubble up and cause the async job to error out instead of handling the failure gracefully (e.g., marking as failed, retrying with backoff intentionally, or providing custom logging/metrics).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — `absolutize_urls` treats protocol-relative URLs (e.g. `//evil.com/x`) as root-relative via `start_with?('/')`, producing a mangled URL (`prefix + "/" + "evil.com/x"`) instead of leaving it absolute or handling it correctly (confidence 65, P3).

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links/images are rewritten when the attribute value `start_with?('/')`. This condition also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//evil.com/x`. The code then does `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, turning `//evil.com/x` into `evil.com/x`, and prefixes it with the source page’s `prefix` (e.g. `http://source.com/evil.com/x`), which is incorrect/mangles what was already an absolute (protocol-relative) URL. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34-35 — if both `i.link` and `i.id` are blank/non-http, the resulting url fails the regex check inside `TopicEmbed.import` and the item is silently skipped with no logging, so failed imports are unobservable (confidence 50, P3).

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, each item’s URL is derived as `url = i.link` and then replaced with `i.id` if `link` is blank or not http(s). That replacement can still yield a blank or non-http(s) value. `TopicEmbed.import` immediately `return`s unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so such items will be skipped. PollFeed neither checks the return value nor logs/records failures, so missed imports due to malformed/blank/non-http URLs are silent and hard to observe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content.scrub` calls String#scrub, which was only added in Ruby 2.1 (Dec 2013), but the Gemfile targets Ruby 1.9/2.0 ("perftools only works on 1.9 atm"), so this will raise NoMethodError on every feed poll under the app's actual runtime. confidence:75 severity:P1

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the diff introduces `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. `String#scrub` is a Ruby core method that only exists on Ruby >= 2.1; on Ruby 1.9.x/2.0 it raises `NoMethodError`. The repository provides evidence it still targets older Rubies (e.g., Gemfile comment about 1.9 compatibility), and nothing in the diff updates the Ruby requirement or adds a backport gem, so this is a concrete runtime-compatibility defect if the app runs on Ruby < 2.1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — confidence 75/P0: `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|` was added retroactively to an already-applied migration (only whitespace/name changed otherwise), so re-running or replaying it (redo, fresh restore replaying schema_migrations mismatch, manual rerun) will silently DROP the existing top_topics table and lose all cached topic ranking data instead of being a no-op.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing (already-dated) migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` causes the table to be dropped and recreated if it already exists. While `schema_migrations` prevents this migration from re-running in normal `db:migrate`, it *will* drop the table during `db:migrate:redo`, rollback+rerun, or any manual re-execution of the migration, causing loss of any existing `top_topics` data. This risk is directly introduced by the change shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — confidence 50/P2: editing the body of a migration that has already run breaks migration content-integrity assumptions (checksums/expectations other devs or CI have of that file), risking divergent schemas across environments that already ran the original version without force: true.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify an existing migration (adds `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`). However, Rails does not enforce migration file checksums by default, and this change does not alter the intended schema when running migrations normally (the table shouldn’t already exist when this migration runs). The only behavioral difference is dropping/recreating the table if it already exists, which is not shown to be a real scenario in this diff. The claim about “content-integrity assumptions/checksums” and divergent schemas is therefore speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — confidence 50/P2: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true do |t|` is safe on first run since the table is new, but force: true means any future accidental re-run (redo, migrate:reset replay, or manual dup) will drop and recreate topic_embeds without warning, discarding any data already stored there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:29 — `ensure_embeddable` authorizes the request by comparing `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but the Referer header is fully client-controlled (trivially spoofed with curl/any non-browser client or a stripped/forged header), so this is not a real access boundary despite acting as the sole auth check for the embed endpoint; confidence 90, severity P2.

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` gates access solely on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and then sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`). Because this before_filter is the only access control shown for `GET /embed/best`, a caller can bypass the intended restriction by supplying a forged Referer header, and the endpoint can trigger side effects (enqueuing `:retrieve_topic`).
